events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 3 points
events.body:
→ D1: A tap alone proves nothing: the same fact records that at the moment of the tap the driver was 613 m from the pickup (F5), and NS-1 requires the tap to be made while GPS shows the driver at the pickup point — a condition the record contradicts, and the platform never logged any arrival at all (F4). [F5 F4 F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D2: Account history does not decide this case: the finding rests on GPS and timeline records (F1, F5, F4), and the driver's profile in fact shows 2 disputes and 2 upheld no-show findings in the last 90 days (F19), which supports our separate flag request rather than his defence. [F19 F18 F1 F5] [NS-1 RD-6]
→ D3: Band 3 (20–29 km/h) is not severe congestion and cannot exempt anything — RD-4(b) bands only corroborate, and only bands 1–2 qualify there; with no incident recorded near the route (F16), the platform correctly flagged the jam claim as unsupported (F22), so it cannot explain stopping 613 m away. [F14 F15 F16 F22] [RD-4 NS-1]

claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 while GPS placed him 613 m from the Victoria St pickup point, far outside any plausible arrival radius, and the platform never once recorded him at the pickup point (driver_arrived_at is null); the arrival condition of the no-show rule therefore fails.

The driver never came within 200 m of the pickup at any time — his closest approach all trip was 612 m at 08:15:30 — so the requirement that he be at the pickup location according to GPS data when claiming arrival was not met.

After tapping "I'm Here" the driver spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup (he remained parked 613 m away from 08:13:10 to 08:19:30), so the required continuous >3-minute wait at the pickup point did not occur and the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee is not chargeable.

The rider was at the named meeting point and said so: at 08:14 she wrote "I'm waiting at the Victoria St entrance of Bugis Junction", and at 08:17 "I'm at the entrance and I don't see any car", while the driver's only reply was the unsupported "I'm here already, please come out" — so the record shows a waiting rider, not a no-show rider.

The driver's account that "Victoria Street was jammed solid, I could not get any closer" is contradicted by the system records: Victoria Street was speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incident recorded anywhere near the route, and the platform itself flagged the claim as unsupported, so it cannot excuse a failure to reach the pickup point.

The driver's post-trip claim of waiting more than 3 minutes is unsupported: GPS shows 0 min 0 s inside the 200 m radius, and the platform logged the bad-faith signals ARRIVAL_LOCATION_MISMATCH and WAIT_CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED against him.
Because NS-1's arrival, location and continuous-wait requirements all fail, the $6.61 cancellation fee charged to the rider must be refunded in full; the fee actually charged is on record as $6.61.

The driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS put him outside the pickup radius, which is precisely the abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-button conduct that warrants a separate account review; his profile shows 2 disputes and 2 upheld no-show findings in 90 days, supporting a flag as additional action (not as the basis of the finding itself).

weaknesses: The rider's own messages (F8, F10) are chat statements and the rider's exact position at the pickup point is not independently corroborated by GPS — the rider-side track is not in the fact table, so the judge must rely on the driver-side GPS records (F1, F5) plus the complaint.

The driver did tap "I'm Here" and did spend 6 min 20 s stationary (F2) and cancelled at 08:19:30 (F3); the other side will argue this shows a genuine wait attempt, though the stationary position was 613 m from the pickup and the 3-minute in-radius condition of NS-1(iii) is still unmet (F5).

The 612/613 m figures come from the driver-side GPS closest approach (F1) and stationary point (F2); if the track had a coverage gap near the pickup the radius test could be contested, though nothing in the record shows such a gap and F4 records no arrival at all.

claims.assertion: The driver did tap the arrival button: the timeline records a driver tap of "I'm Here" at 08:16:00 (F5), so the arrival step of the cancellation policy was performed and this is not a case of a driver who never signalled arrival.

The driver is a long-standing, high-volume, well-rated partner: 700 days on the platform, 540 trips in the last 90 days and a 4.6 rating (F19); the rider also has a clean record (F18), so no bad faith is imputed to either party's account history in this case.

The driver's claim that Victoria Street was jammed solid (F13) is partly corroborated by the traffic record: Victoria Street was in speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) during 08:00–08:30 (F14), i.e. slow though not severe, with no incident recorded nearby (F16) and fair weather (F17).

weaknesses: The GPS record destroys the arrival and waiting claims: the driver never came within 200 m of the pickup — closest approach 612 m at 08:15:30, and 613 m from the pickup at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap (F1, F5), with 0 seconds inside the radius after the tap (F5). On NS-1 (ii) and (iii) this fails outright and the $6.61 must be refunded under NS-2.

The timeline further records the platform never logging the driver at the pickup point at all (F4, driver_arrived_at is null), and flags two high/medium bad-faith signals — ARRIVAL_LOCATION_MISMATCH (F20) and WAIT_CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED (F21) — which NS-2 expressly ties to a flag_account for misuse of the arrival/waiting button.

The driver's congestion excuse is contradicted by the system record: the JAM_CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED signal notes speed bands on record are all ≥ 20 km/h and no incident was recorded (F22, F16), and RD-4(b) bands only corroborate and never exempt on their own; band 3 is above the band 1–2 severe-congestion range (F14, F15).

The driver's written statement that the rider never showed up (F13) is a statement contradicted by GPS and by the rider's own messages asking where the car was and for the plate number (F8, F10), and statements lose to system records.
The driver's message "I'm here already, please come out" (F9) was sent at 08:16 while GPS placed the car 613 m away (F1, F5): the chat content cannot be used to support an arrival finding.

points.response: A tap alone proves nothing: the same fact records that at the moment of the tap the driver was 613 m from the pickup (F5), and NS-1 requires the tap to be made while GPS shows the driver at the pickup point — a condition the record contradicts, and the platform never logged any arrival at all (F4).

Account history does not decide this case: the finding rests on GPS and timeline records (F1, F5, F4), and the driver's profile in fact shows 2 disputes and 2 upheld no-show findings in the last 90 days (F19), which supports our separate flag request rather than his defence.

Band 3 (20–29 km/h) is not severe congestion and cannot exempt anything — RD-4(b) bands only corroborate, and only bands 1–2 qualify there; with no incident recorded near the route (F16), the platform correctly flagged the jam claim as unsupported (F22), so it cannot explain stopping 613 m away.

Conceded on the arrival condition: F5 puts the "I'm Here" tap at 08:16:00 while GPS placed the car 613 m from the pickup, F4 records no platform arrival at all, and on NS-1 (i)–(ii) the arrival requirement is not met.
Conceded: F1 and F2 are consistent — the closest approach was 612 m at 08:15:30 and the car sat 613 m away at (1.2958, 103.8495), so he was never inside the pickup radius, and NS-2 therefore applies.
Conceded: 0 s inside the radius after the tap (F5) means the continuous >3-minute in-radius wait required by NS-1 (iii) did not occur, and the $6.61 fee is not chargeable under NS-2.

Conceded: F8 and F10 show a rider waiting at the named Victoria St entrance and asking for the plate, and F9 was sent while the car was 613 m away (F1, F5), so the record shows a waiting rider rather than a genuine no-show.

The driver's statement (F13) is contradicted by the system records: Victoria Street was band 3 / 20–29 km/h (F14), North Bridge Road likewise (F15), with no incident recorded (F16) and fair weather (F17), and RD-4(b) bands could never exempt on their own — which is exactly why this defence fails and the outcome is a refund; my brief had already recorded this as a bad-faith signal (F22).

Accepted as against my client: the post-trip wait claim (F11, F13) is unsupported by the GPS record of 0 s within 200 m (F5), and the platform's ARRIVAL_LOCATION_MISMATCH and WAIT_CLAIM_UNSUPPORTED signals (F20, F21) stand as recorded.

Agreed, and it is what I ask for: the fee on record is $6.61 (F3, F6) with no surge (F7), and since NS-1 (i)–(iii) fail the rider pays nothing, so refund_full of $6.61 under NS-2 is the correct disposal of this case between the parties.

The refund does not depend on the flag, and the only record of a repeated pattern is F19's two upheld no-show disputes in 90 days; if the court treats the mis-tap as the NS-2 trigger it should be told plainly that the tap was a driver-performed action (F5) and not a platform auto-arrival (F4), which is the fact that makes the flag arguable — I ask the court to note the driver's 700-day, 540-trip, 4.6-rated history (F19) when weighing it.
